raw_response:
I have farmed these 5 mu in Quzhou County for 50 years. At 69, my back is not what it used to be, and my sons work off-farm in the city, so my wife and I handle most of the daily work. I know this soil and the local market well. I will plant hybrid seeds for all four crops because the old traditional varieties cannot stand up to the diseases here anymore, and buyers pay better for uniform produce. I use rotary tillage to save fuel and labor—deep ploughing is too hard on me now. 

I split the land so that chili and kidney bean, which are a bit easier on my aging body, take 1.5 mu each, while cucumber and eggplant, which need more attention but fetch higher prices, take 1 mu each. I have reliable well water, so I will irrigate more often for cucumber because it is thirsty, and about 5 times for chili and kidney bean. I will spray pesticides regularly—about 10 to 15 times per crop—because aphids, spider mites, and fungi will ruin the whole harvest if I get lazy. For fertilizer, I will lay down compound fertilizer as basal dressing and top-dress with urea and special vegetable fertilizers. I still keep part of my cabbage-chili-cabbage rotation in mind for soil health, but this year my main effort goes into these four cash crops.
